maria: FYI ran an int8/int6 bring-up on the new small-dim model against the standard holdout set :chart_with_downwards_trend: 

maria: quick summary - recall@1/5/10 (float32 / int8 / int6): 0.723 / 0.705 / 0.657  | recall@10: 0.902 / 0.887 / 0.843
maria: silhouette (cosine) float32 0.211 -> int8 0.197 -> int6 0.145  (UMAP shows tail clusters getting noisy)

alex: thanks — what's the eval harness & sample size? :eyes:

maria: ran 50k queries sampled stratified by freq (head/longtail/short). eval script: 
```
python eval/emb_eval.py \n  --model pelican-small-int6 \n  --holdout data/holdout_v2.jsonl \n  --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette,cosine_shift \n  --batch-size 1024
```

sam: did you use per-channel quant or symmetric per-tensor?

maria: per-channel with 8-bit calibration for int8, and a 6-bit per-channel clamp run for int6 (linear symmetric). calibration used 10k calibration samples from the training corpus.

jing: did you change normalization pipeline? we recently toggled l2-norm-before-avg in the featurizer, that can affect cosine distances a lot.

maria: good call — I re-ran with l2 normalization ON (same as float32 baseline). if we switch to postnorm the silhouette drop is slightly larger.

alex: can you paste the cosine-shift distribution? interested in tail mass.

maria: attached quick summary numbers inline: median cosine shift (float32->quant): int8 0.007, int6 0.028; 95th pctile shift: int8 0.035, int6 0.12. tail >0.1 mostly longtail queries.

sam: longtail hit makes sense. int6 noise seems to collapse small clusters — that explains silhouette drop. did you try per-channel zero-point adjustments / asymmetric quant?

maria: not yet. plan: run asymmetric per-channel + minmax clipping sweep next. also try fine-tune-aware quant (post-training quant with bias correction) on a 1% subset.

eval-bot: CI: emb-eval job 1711023456 finished — artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/pelican-small/1711023456/ (recall_report.csv, umap_samples.png) :white_check_mark:

jing: please add a small qualitative check — nearest neighbor samples for a handful of longtail queries. last time int6 flipped nearest neighbour labels for ~12% of those.

maria: yep will run NN diff dump and a small manual review. plan timeline: asymmetric sweep by EOD tomorrow, NN diff + qualitative review by Thu.

alex: if asymmetric helps we can consider int6 for cold storage index (low-cost) but keep int8 for online recall. agree on manual review before any rollout. :+1:

sam: also try tiny calibration set with per-output-channel scaling (we saw wins on centroids in previous run).

maria: adding that to the sweep. will post results in this thread and attach the recall/UMAP artifacts.

alex: awesome — thanks. once we have the NN diffs, let's decide fallback policy (index-time re-embed vs runtime fallback to int8).

maria: noted. cc @alex @jing @sam for follow-ups.
